planted.case: the linear-kernel solve equals FoldSolver at the 11 shared penalties
a non-linear code: the kernel decoder reads it, the linear one does not
lost information: neither decoder reads more than the token holds
a token that holds only time: its kernel score against the clock floor (recorded)

rule.scores: per encoder, window part, body, target and decoder: the decoder's best cross-validated content score (1 - squared error / squared deviation of the part's target about its mean; 0 = no better than the part's mean target, 1 = exact)
rule.ruled_parts: the 4 parts of window 484,675 and parts 2-4 of window 489,350 (its part 1 shares 265 of its 300 samples with window 484,675's part 4 and is left out by encoder_check.excluded_parts): 7 parts, body 1's lower trunk at -142 to -166 degrees
rule.paired_difference: the later encoder's score minus the earlier encoder's, per ruled part, per body
rule.lower: body 1 reads LOWER under a decoder and target when encoder_check's question-1 rule (rule_reading) on its 7 paired differences reads 'later encoder lower' (lower on at least 6 of 7 AND the 97.5% upper bound of the mean paired difference, t with 6 degrees of freedom, below 0) AND its mean paired difference is below the lowest of bodies 2-8's mean paired differences (the reference band: bodies 2-8 read the same way)
rule.unreadable: linear: a ruled part's best at either end of its penalty grid for either encoder (encoder_check.curve_rule); kernel: a ruled part's best at either end of K_LAMS or at the smallest c (the most local kernel) for either encoder. A kernel best at the largest c (the smoothest kernel, nearest a low-order polynomial ridge whose linear limit the linear decoder reads) is read and counted
rule.clock: the clock clause: body 1's kernel score with the later encoder above the clock floor (the encoder-free kernel decoder on the samples' time index, same part, body and target) on at least 6 of the 7 ruled parts
rule.primary: model@489350 against model@481800 (the last encoder before the loss's onset; the trajectory row's and MECHANISM.md's reference)
reading: PREMISE: the linear decoder reads body 1 LOWER on world_posture (the registered loss reproduced against 481,800). If not: 'premise not reproduced' and nothing below is read.

LOST INFORMATION: the kernel decoder also reads body 1 LOWER on world_posture. Then: kernel LOWER on heading_free_posture = 'lost posture information' (the body's configuration); kernel not LOWER on heading_free_posture but LOWER on heading = 'lost heading'; neither = 'lost, not attributed to configuration or heading'.

NON-LINEAR CODE (no information lost): the kernel decoder does not read body 1 LOWER on world_posture (within its spread across parts, within bodies 2-8's band, or higher) AND the clock clause holds on world_posture.
NOT DECIDED BY THE TOKEN: the kernel decoder does not read body 1 LOWER on world_posture but the clock clause fails (the kernel score does not exceed what the samples' time alone gives).
UNREADABLE: the linear or the kernel reading on world_posture is unreadable (a best at a grid end, above).
rule.beside: the same rule for model@489350 against frozen@481100 and against model@484675, model@484675 against model@481800, model@481800 against frozen@481100; the rule on each ruled window alone (its 4 parts); window 479,350 (the turn from -77 to -134 degrees): whole-window and per-part scores per encoder; the best of the two decoders per reading; all deciding nothing
rule.consequence: LOST INFORMATION: a defect to repair; the separating run from 481,800 (the review's computation 3) decides its cause. NON-LINEAR CODE: no posture information lost on these rows; the loss lives in the linear read-out only, and the separating run is not needed for an information defect
